subtype: Colleague who is reliable rather than brilliant [Observer]
passage: In the Berlin translation office, the Thursday report arrived at four o'clock, always from Selin, always short and clear. Kofi had watched it for months. Marek, the star of the team, had once turned around a whole client glossary overnight and everyone clapped, but then he vanished for two weeks and his tasks stayed open. When the big contract came, the team lead handed the schedule to Selin without much discussion. "I know she'll tell me on Thursday if something slips," the lead said. Nobody asked Marek. Kofi wondered whether Selin even knew how much trust had built up, week by week, out of small reports. Selin just nodded and opened the calendar.

qa.q: At what time did Selin's report arrive each Thursday?
qa.a: Selin's report arrived at four o'clock.

qa.q: What was Kofi feeling and wondering as the lead gave the schedule to Selin?
qa.a: Kofi felt quietly impressed and curious, wondering whether Selin knew how much trust the small weekly reports had built.

qa.q: What could a star like Marek do to earn the same trust?
qa.a: Deliver something small every week and say early when something slips, so the team can count on him.

qa.q: How might Selin experience being chosen without much discussion?
qa.a: Probably quietly pleased and maybe surprised, since the choice came from steady weekly habits and not from one big moment.

grounding: Illustrates a team noticing that a quiet team member's steady weekly delivery earns more trust than a star who disappears.

subtype: Colleague who is reliable rather than brilliant [Observer]
passage: In the staff room of the city school, Madhav counted the Monday sheets pinned to the board: eleven in a row from Indu, each with attendance and pending fees in the same neat columns. Rohit, the art teacher, had painted the whole annual-day backdrop in one weekend and got applause, but for the next fortnight his register stayed blank and other teachers covered his classes. When the principal needed someone to plan the exam duty roster, she looked at the board, then at Indu. "You have never missed a Monday," she said. Indu blinked, then tucked her pen away. That evening Madhav took out his own diary and wrote down one small thing he could deliver every single week.

qa.q: How many Monday sheets did Madhav count on the board?
qa.a: Madhav counted eleven Monday sheets in a row from Indu.

qa.q: What was Madhav feeling as he wrote one small weekly commitment in his diary?
qa.a: Inspired and a little self-critical, having seen steady delivery earn trust. 😊

qa.q: What could Rohit do to become as trusted as Indu?
qa.a: Rohit could make small regular contributions, such as keeping his register filled every week, and not only big weekend bursts.

qa.q: How might Indu have felt when the principal mentioned the Monday sheets?
qa.a: Surprised, as the blink shows, and possibly pleased to learn that the steady sheets counted.

grounding: Illustrates colleagues noticing that the quiet person delivering every week is trusted over the star who vanishes and reappears.
